text: Tribunal hearings are an effective way to solve certain civil disputes.
Explain how tribunals operate and consider whether this statement is true. Illustrate your answer
with examples. [25]
Bernhardt has been charged with the theft of a gold bracelet worth £2000 (theft is a triable either
way offence).
Describe the process through which Bernhardt’s case will pass from his first appearance in court
to the conclusion of his trial. Discuss the decisions that will have to be made about the court in
which he is to be tried. [25]
Explain how jurors are selected. Critically consider what arguments could be put forward in favour
of the abolition of juries in both civil and criminal cases. [25]
The decision in Pepper v Hart (1993) is a clear indication that courts are now moving towards a
more purposive approach to statutory interpretation.
Describe the various tools and approaches available to judges and evaluate the accuracy of this
statement. [25]
Describe the development of Equity and discuss its relevance today. [25]
Since 1990 there have been many changes to the legal profession.
Critically discuss whether these changes have improved provision of legal services. [25]
